message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “soft” card because it can be counted as either **1** or **11**, depending on which value gives your hand the best chance of winning without going over 21.

- **If counting the Ace as 11 keeps your total ≤ 21, you’ll usually use 11.**  
- **If using 11 would make you bust (> 21), the Ace automatically drops to 1.**

So an Ace is flexible: it starts as 11 but can switch to 1 whenever necessary. This flexibility also applies to multiple Aces—one will normally be 11 while the others become 1 unless you’re still under 21.

Just explain that Ace can count as 1 or 11, whichever benefits the hand without busting; if both values cause bust, it's counted as 1. Also mention that if you have two Aces, one counts as 11 and the other as 1 unless you bust. Also mention that Ace can be used as a natural 21 (blackjack) when combined with a ten-value card. Also mention that some casinos treat Ace as 11 only until you bust, then it becomes 1. So we just give a concise explanation.
